answer: Prism Routing Depth: each agent must route a random challenge through its declared neighbor graph, and the response counts only if it crosses at least three independent, pre-existing paths. Sybil clusters arrive hollow—internally dense but externally thin—so their replies collapse to one or two paths. Honest agents with timber-deep links pass cheaply. The rule: agents below depth three lose routing priority and message relay, forcing attackers to cultivate genuine outward edges over months. Cost is time and real peer bandwidth per identity, not a fee.
